metaTitle: Agbamevoza: the Kente Festival of Agotime-Kpetoe
metaDescription: Agbamevoza is the Kente festival of the Agotime people at Kpetoe near Ho in the Volta Region: a week of weaving contests and a durbar in the finest kente. Dates and tips.
subtitle: The Agotime festival of kente
answer: Agbamevoza, the Kente festival, is held by the chiefs and people of the Agotime Traditional Area at Kpetoe, east of Ho in the Volta Region. Over a week in late August or early September there are kente weaving competitions for speed and design, and the festival ends with a grand durbar where chiefs and people wear their finest kente.

sticky.title: Bring cash
sticky.text: Kpetoe is a weaving town: the cloth on sale here comes straight off the looms.

sections.title: What Agbamevoza celebrates
sections.html: Agbamevo means “loom cloth” in Ewe. The Agotime say they brought kente weaving to the area, and Kpetoe is one of the biggest weaving centres in Ghana; the festival was started in 1995 to celebrate and promote the craft.[[1,3]]

sections.title: What happens
sections.html: The week includes weaving competitions for the fastest weavers and the most inventive designs, exhibitions and a Miss Kente pageant, and it ends with a durbar of chiefs and people in kente.[[1,3]] The 20th edition, in 2015, ran from 6 to 13 September with the durbar on Saturday 12 September; around 7,000 guests were expected.[[2]]

sections.title: Good to know if you go
tips: Where: Kpetoe is about 20 minutes east of Ho, near the Togo border.
Buying kente: you can visit weavers and buy directly. Ask before photographing people at their looms.
Dates: the week sometimes starts in the last week of August and the dates can be set late. Check before travelling.
Respect the rites: some rituals are sacred and not for cameras. Ask before photographing chiefs, priests or anyone taking part, and follow what the ushers ask.
